title: The Lobster Nephew
logline: Marshall finally gets jury duty and becomes the lone holdout in Halvorsen v. Pappas: forty-one years of Thursday lunches, one skipped Thursday, one nephew sent in his place, and one thirty-eight-fifty diner lobster. While Ted, Robin and Barney discover they are terrible at being Marshall, the sequestered jury is marched into the restaurant where Marshall's own stand-in is on date night with Lily, in Marshall's flannel, ordering the lobster on her week.
coldOpen: Kids, in all his years as a lawyer, your Uncle Marshall only argued one case he truly believed in. He wasn't the lawyer. He was juror number four.

guests.name: Doreen Mulvaney
guests.role: Jury foreperson, thirty-four years a clerk at the Manhattan DMV; runs deliberations like the DMV, calls every juror by number ('Now serving juror number four'), and has never once believed anyone's thing was a big deal

guests.name: Trent Belfiore
guests.role: Juror number three, a hedge-fund analyst in a fleece vest with courtside Knicks tickets at seven thirty; will vote for whichever side gets him out the door, and blurts out anything that might cause a mistrial

guests.name: Herb Albrecht
guests.role: Juror number six, eighty-eight, has served on fourteen juries and slept through every one; wakes up only to say one short thing about lunch or nephews, and is always right

scenes.summary: Wednesday. Marshall's jury summons finally comes, and he's thrilled; everyone else brags about how they got out of it (Barney winks at the defendant, Robin's Canadian, Ted corrected the judge's pronunciation of voir dire, Lily threatened the time-out chair). Thursday is date night, seventeen years unbroken, and Lily's week to pay. Just in case, Marshall hands out his In Case of Jury card: Robin moves the Fiero (it only starts if you sincerely tell it it's a good car), Ted gives his summer-associates speech from a card that just says 'Tell them about the ice house' (even Lily doesn't know what that is), and under no circumstances Barney. Button: what could take more than an hour?

beats.line: It started on a Wednesday, with the best mail Marshall had ever gotten.
Guys. It came. My jury summons. Tomorrow, nine a.m.
Oh no. I'm so sorry.
Sorry? Robin, this is the Super Bowl of citizenship. I've been waiting twelve years.
I've been summoned eleven times. Never served once.
How?
I tell the judge I can spot a liar from across the room. Then I wink at the defendant.
Dismissed in four minutes. Once the defendant asked me out.
I'm Canadian. We don't really do juries. We just ask the guy if he did it, and he apologizes.
I got dismissed during voir dire.
For what?
For correcting how the judge pronounced voir dire.
He also held Ted in contempt.
Which, to be fair, he pronounced beautifully.
I told them I teach kindergarten, and the defendant would sit in my time-out chair until he confessed.
Lily!
It was a parking ticket. He cracked in eleven minutes.
You people disgust me. A jury is the one room in a courthouse where nobody's billing anybody.
I've seen Twelve Angry Men thirty-one times. I cry when the old man changes his vote. Every time.
Even the times you fell asleep?
I cry in my sleep, Ted.
Just remember tomorrow is Thursday.
Date night. Seventeen years of Thursdays. Never missed one.
And it's my week to pay, so I'm getting the good wine.
Lilypad, you always get the good wine on your week.
That's what makes it my week.
Anyway, I'll be done by lunch. But just in case, I made assignments.
Under no circumstances, Barney.
beats.title: In Case of Jury
lines: 11:30. Move the Fiero. Street cleaning. Robin.
8:00. Date night. Me. Nobody else. Especially not Barney.

beats.line: Why especially not Barney?
Because you'd do it.
I would absolutely do it.
Robin. The Fiero only starts if you tell her she's a good car.
No.
And you have to mean it. She can tell.
Ted, my speech. Why I became a lawyer. It's all on one card.
It just says, tell them about the ice house.
What ice house? We've been together seventeen years. I've never heard of an ice house.
You won't need it. It's some little civil case. What could possibly take more than an hour?
Fourteen hours, kids. Fourteen hours, over thirty-eight dollars and fifty cents.

scenes.summary: The jury room. Halvorsen v. Pappas: forty-one years of Thursday lunches at the Acropolis Diner, alternating who pays, until Pappas skipped one, wouldn't say why, and sent his nephew Dino, who ordered the diner's never-ordered lobster on Halvorsen's week. Five to one for Pappas; Marshall holds out. Cutaway: how Marshall pictures it, with himself as Halvorsen and Barney as the nephew ('It's my week.' 'I know.'). Doreen has seen too many big deals at the DMV, jurors two and five have transferred to a murder trial because it's more relaxing, and Marshall reenacts the nephew's nine-second walk to the lobster. The judge sequesters them. Marshall's one call: Lily won't wait for a stand-in, she'll take one, and she hangs up on 'not Barney'. Herb wakes: who's Barney? The nephew.

beats.line: The case was Halvorsen versus Pappas. The first vote took four minutes.
Five for Pappas. One for Halvorsen. Now serving juror number four.
Thank you. Hi. I'm Marshall. I'd like to talk about the lobster.
No. Nope. I have Knicks tickets.
It's ten forty in the morning.
They're good seats. I like to get there early and look at them.
Arne Halvorsen and Gus Pappas. Lunch every Thursday at the Acropolis Diner for forty-one years. They take turns paying.
Then one Thursday, Halvorsen's week, Pappas doesn't show. He sends his nephew, Dino.
And Dino orders the lobster.
The lobster! It's been on that menu since 1972. Nobody has ever ordered it. It's a diner!
Halvorsen paid. Thirty-eight fifty. He wants it back. That's the whole case.
And Pappas won't even say why he skipped.
He took the Fifth. On lunch.
Juror six has been asleep since opening statements.
I heard everything.
What's the case about?
Lunch.
Forty-one years. And he sends a nephew. I can see it so clearly.
Forty-one years, Gus. Where are you?
Uncle Gus sends his regrets. I'm Dino.
Waiter! The lobster. And I'm keeping the bib.
Nobody orders the lobster!
Forty-one years nobody's ordered it. It's been waiting for me.
But it's my week.
I know.
Sorry. In my head, the nephew is my friend Barney.
Why?
Because Barney would absolutely order the lobster.
Dude. They're eighty years old. It's thirty-eight dollars. Let it go.
It's not thirty-eight dollars. It's a Thursday.
Sir. Thirty-four years at the DMV. Every person who came to my window thought their thing was a big deal.
None of them were.
Have none of you seen Twelve Angry Men?
There are four of us.
Where are jurors two and five?
They asked to be moved. They're on a murder trial now. They said it's more relaxing.
Dino testified he walked from the door to the table and ordered without opening a menu. I'd like to reenact it.
Please don't.
Forty-one feet. Time me.
Nine seconds. He never looked at a menu. He came for the lobster!
Or he was hungry!
Or he was a nephew. I've got eleven nephews. Every one of them would order the lobster.
By five o'clock, it was still five to one. Then the judge sent a note.
No verdict tonight, we're sequestered. Dinner on the court, then a motel in Queens.
Sequestered? For thirty-eight fifty?
He says it's the principle.
I love this judge.
Courtside, man! I've been practicing for the kiss cam!
Lilypad. It's me. They're sequestering us.
No, it's not a sex thing.
I know. Seventeen years. But the streak doesn't have to die. Somebody can take you, and it still counts.
Who are you taking?
Not Barney. Lily. Lily, not Barney.
She hung up.
Who's Barney?
He's the nephew.

scenes.summary: Thursday evening. Robin wouldn't lie to a car, so the Fiero got towed with her in it. Ted didn't know what the ice house was, so he gave Marshall's 'why I became a lawyer' speech about igloos, and three summer associates quit law; Judy wouldn't tell Lily about the ice house either. Ted and Robin both offer to be Lily's date-night stand-in; Lily, evil, picks the worst one on purpose. Barney enters in Marshall's red flannel and khakis: 'Haaave you met Marshall?' He's had a key to the apartment since 2006, and a Playbook play called The Eriksen. Lily warns him it's her week: order something reasonable. Button: 'Flannel up.'

beats.line: Meanwhile, the rest of us were learning that being Marshall was a lot harder than it looked.
Okay. Report. How did being my husband go?
The Fiero got towed.
Did you tell her she's a good car?
I'm not going to lie to a car, Lily.
I tried the key. I tried jumper cables. I tried yelling at it in French.
They towed it with me inside. All the way to the impound lot in Queens. We didn't speak.
Ted. Summer associates?
Well, the card said, tell them about the ice house. Which, again, what ice house?
I called his mother. She said if he never told me, he didn't want me to know. Then she hung up.
So I improvised. I told them about the greatest ice house ever built. The igloo.
No beams. No mortar. Every block holds up every other block. Fifty minutes. They were rapt.
Ted, it was supposed to make them want to be lawyers.
Three of them quit law to study architecture.
One still wants to be a lawyer. He wants to sue me.
And now Marshall wants a stand-in for date night, so the streak still counts.
I'm free. I'll take you.
I'll go. I owe him for the Fiero.
No. If my husband sends me a stand-in, I'm taking the worst one.
Lily, he specifically said not Barney.
I know.
Lilypad! Sorry I'm late. I stopped to cry at a dog.
Is that Marshall's flannel?
Haaave you met Marshall?
Where did you even get his clothes?
His closet. I've had a key to that apartment since 2006.
Why?
Please.
Wait. Uncle Barney had a key to your apartment?
We changed the locks four times, Penny. He had a key to all four.
Step five. Bigfoot. Mean it.
beats.title: The Eriksen
lines: Order a second entree for the table. Eat it.

beats.line: Fine. But it's my week to pay. So you order something reasonable.
Lilypad. When have I ever let you down?
Constantly.
Come on, Lilypad. Let's keep a streak alive. Flannel up!

scenes.summary: Sorrento's, Marshall and Lily's date-night spot. Barney is unsettlingly good at being Marshall, and physically can't say anything dumb. The sequestered jury is marched in on a court coupon; Doreen forbids contact with the outside world, which is Lily. Barney orders the lobster on Lily's week ('I know.'), Herb wakes for 'nephews', and Marshall realizes he's Pappas. Lily corners the foreperson, Trent blurts the whole case hoping for a mistrial, and Lily: 'You sent a nephew.' Why can't he let it go? The ice house: the eighty-dollar fishing shack that sank, three St. Cloud lawyers who laughed at his dad, the quiet drive home, and the lawyer Marshall meant to be before the bank. The jurors flip one by one; verdict for Halvorsen. Marshall takes his own chair back and pays: thirty-eight fifty plus every Thursday for life. Lily: then every week's her week. Robin sprang the Fiero by telling it she loved it, which Ted takes personally. Future Ted: Pappas's reason.

beats.line: Lilypad, you look like a sunrise over Lake Minnetonka.
That's actually really close.
Sorry. Give me a second. This bread basket is just so beautiful.
Stop it. You're too smooth. Marshall's never this smooth. Say something dumb.
Bigfoot is... I can't. My body won't let me.
Sequestered jury, table for four. The court had a coupon.
Lily?
Juror four. No contact with the outside world.
That's my wife!
She's the outside world.
And that's Barney. In my flannel. In my chair.
Waiter! The lobster, please.
Barney, it's my week!
I know.
Told you. Nephews.
Oh no. I didn't show up for our Thursday. I sent a nephew.
I'm Pappas.
Marshall Eriksen. Seventeen years of Thursdays, and you send me Barney. In your flannel.
Ma'am, you cannot talk to this juror.
Fine. Then I'll talk to you. What's this case about?
Two old guys do lunch every Thursday, one skips, sends his nephew, the nephew orders the lobster on the other guy's week.
Juror three!
What? Mistrial, I make the fourth quarter.
You sent a nephew.
Marshall, it's thirty-eight dollars. Why can't you let it go? Is this the ice house?
When I was ten, a guy sold my dad an ice-fishing house. Eighty bucks. First day on the lake, it sank.
Into the ice?
Into the ice. The one thing it was for.
Dad went to three lawyers in St. Cloud. All three laughed at him. The third one charged him for it.
Dad laughed too. Dad laughs at everything. But on the drive home, he didn't turn on the radio.
So I decided I'd be the lawyer who doesn't laugh. The one who takes the eighty-dollar case.
Then I went to work for a bank. Now I bill four hundred an hour to laugh at guys with ice houses.
Today's the first time in eight years anybody asked me what's fair. I just didn't want it to be over.
Marshmallow. Why didn't you ever tell me?
Because it's the only story where my dad loses.
Halvorsen.
Lily. The old man changed his vote.
Because of the ice house?
Fourteen juries. First time I ever stayed awake.
Halvorsen. Thirty-four years at that window. Yours is the first big deal.
Halvorsen. Can I go now?
Jurors two and five?
They texted. They'll vote whichever way makes the big guy stop talking.
Then we have a verdict. Now serving: everyone's dinner.
Barney. You're the nephew. Out of my chair.
Lilypad. The lobster's on me. Thirty-eight fifty, plus damages.
What are the damages?
Every Thursday, for the rest of our lives, I pay.
So every week is my week.
Barney. Get the good wine.
I got the Fiero out. I told her she's a good car. I told her I loved her.
She started right up. I hate that it worked.
It took me a whole year to get that out of you.
You're not a good car.
Halvorsen got his thirty-eight fifty, and Marshall never missed another Thursday.
Years later, he finally asked Pappas why he'd skipped that one. Jury duty. Lone holdout. On a sandwich.
